Subject: Slate run: coordinating hands-on POC, redaction checklist, and load-test window

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for committing engineering time for the hands-on POC. We propose a two-part slate run next week: a 90-minute prompt-review + routing test, followed immediately by a 60-minute load test (synthetic traffic). Goal: validate prompt handling, routing fallback, and steady-state throughput.

Quick ask before we lock the calendar: could you share a small sample set (10–20 representative prompts) and a redaction priority list for any PII we should remove? If you prefer, we can provision a sanitized sample on our side and hand it back to you to confirm. I attached a short redaction-checklist and a CSV template for sample prompts.

Proposed windows (PT):
- Tue 2026-08-18, 10:30–12:00
- Wed 2026-08-19, 13:00–14:30 (prompt review) + 14:30–15:30 (load test)
- Thu 2026-08-20, 09:00–10:30

Please tell us which works best and who from Acme will join the prompt walkthrough vs the load-test observation (engineering vs product).

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

—Emily

Thanks,
Rachel

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Emily Park <epark@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 07:44:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: runbook + load-test ramp plan — technical notes

Rachel / Ben — forwarding the runbook summary with a few technical notes for the session:

- Routing: we'll configure a latency-first route to the quantized variant and a cost-fallback to the standard variant if GPU pool is constrained. We'll surface model-switch events in the console.
- KV cache: yes, we'll explicitly flush the KV cache between the prompt-review and the load warmup to avoid warm-state artifacts.
- Load test profile: start at 5 QPS for 5 minutes, step to 20 QPS over 10 minutes, hold a 3-minute steady-state at 20 QPS, then wind down. Payload size: please confirm average token length — we assumed 100 tokens/sample for CPU/GPU planning.
- Test data: please ensure your sample CSV uses the "prompt" column and that any placeholders are bracketed (e.g., [USER_NAME]).

Emily — quick question for planning: can Acme tolerate an intentional latency spike during the 20 QPS steady-state (we'll annotate the runbook and keep an eye on SLOs)? If that needs approval, let us know and we'll omit the steady-state.

Thanks,
Dev
Staff Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
